lesson.title: Campaign Creators
lesson.subtitle: Term 4 Week 3, Session 4
lesson.footer: Persuasive Writing | Year 5/6 Literacy | Week 3 Session 4

plan.curriculum: English 2.0, Level 5: VC2E5LA07 how still images affect meaning; VC2E5LY10 creating multimodal texts for purpose and audience; VC2E5LY08 features used to meet purpose and audience
plan.shape: model, sharpen, design, gallery: the four poster parts modelled, slogans and calls to action sharpened, then each student designs their own poster and a gallery walk tests it, because a visual product re-energises the class before drafting week
plan.criticalFeature: words and picture work together on one message, ending in one small action
decisionPoints: the choice check: the best call to action
the exit board: a new campaign's slogan and action
plan.anchor: Claim it. Prove it. Sell it. A poster does all three in a glance: slogan, fact, picture.
plan.catchUp: Missed the week? Give the Worksheet plan and the issue plastic at the beach. Everything they need is on the slide and the planner.

Sticky notes for the gallery walk

Point to A, B or C
boardSetup: Four poster parts on the board: slogan, picture, key fact, call to action
Space to pin finished posters for the gallery walk

slides.notes: Open the session. One line: today we design posters that could change what people at our school do.

Print the Worksheet for everyone (its last section is the poster plan), the Extension for early finishers and the Supported Worksheet for those who need it. A3 paper and colours on tables. This is the draw and create fun activity.

slides.learningIntention: We are learning to design a campaign poster where words and pictures work together.
successCriteria: I can name the four parts of a campaign poster.
I can write a slogan and a call to action that match my picture.
I can explain how my words and picture work on the reader.

beats: POINT to the learning intention.
SAY: Two seconds to persuade. Let's make them count.
SAY: Read the I can lines with me. Everyone, together, on three.
SAY: Naming the four parts is where we start.
A slogan and action that match the picture is today's main goal.
notes.prep: SC1 naming the parts is reachable for all; SC2 slogan and call to action is the core and the exit evidence; SC3 explaining the word-picture effect is the stretch.

slides.title: What makes you stop and look?
lines: Think of a poster or sign you actually remember.

notes.answer: a big picture, a short catchy line, bright colours, one message
beats: SAY: You walk past hundreds of posters.
A few stick. Why those?
ASK: What made a poster stick for you?
20 sec. Turn and tell, partner A first.
EXPECT: a big picture; a funny or short line; it told me what to do
ASK: Do you read every word on a poster?
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs down
SAY: So a poster has two seconds.
Words and picture must work together on one message.
trap: Fix: ask did you read it all? Student realises it was the picture or the line.
notes.prep: Low-coupling launch; everyone has seen posters. Links Week 2 Sell it and Week 3 devices. 3 minutes.

slides.meaning: A short, catchy line people remember.

notes.answer: a short, catchy line people remember
beats: POINT to the word. SAY: Slogan. Say it with me. Slogan.
SAY: A slogan is short and catchy. You remember it without trying.
No ice, no bears. Four words.
ASK: Tell your partner a slogan you know from an ad or a sign.
10 sec. Turn and tell, partner B first.
EXPECT: Slip, slop, slap; any ad line
trap: a slogan that's a whole sentence of reasons.
Fix: ask can you shout it? Student cuts it to a few words.
notes.prep: Slip, Slop, Slap is the Australian classic most students will know.

rows: My poster: switch off for the Arctic
one polar bear on a tiny piece of ice
Summer sea ice shrinks about 12% a decade (NASA)

notes.answer: slogan, picture, key fact and call to action all on one message
beats: POINT to Slogan.
SAY: Four words, a pattern, easy to remember. Lights off. Ice on.
POINT to Picture.
SAY: One bear, one tiny piece of ice. The picture shows the problem in a glance.
POINT to Call to action.
SAY: Switch off one light tonight. Small and easy. Save the planet is too big.
ASK: Which part is the Prove it?
5 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: the key fact
trap: a poster with three messages: plastic, cars and lights.
Fix: student circles one message and cuts the rest.
notes.stretch: Make the picture tell the story with no words at all.
notes.help: Copy the four-row table, fill one row at a time.
notes.prep: The model. Critical feature: words and picture work together on one message, ending in one small action.

slides.title: Which poster part?
slides.pivot: ask: does it name, show, prove or ask for action?
slides.followUp: cold call one student: how did you know?

items.text: Bring your own cup to the canteen on Friday.
Australia wastes about 7.6 million tonnes of food a year (Australian Government).
Crush it. Can it. Recycle it.

say: 1 slogan, 3 key fact, 4 call to action.
Pictures are 2, but today every line is words.
trap: calling the call to action a slogan because it's short.
Fix: ask does it tell me what to do? Then it's the action.
notes.stretch: Turn the fact into a slogan.
notes.help: Look for a number: that's usually the fact.
notes.prep: Guided naming of the poster parts. SC1. Food waste figure: National Food Waste Baseline, 2021.

slides.title: Shrink the slogan
slides.pivot: find the one key idea, then say it in four words
slides.followUp: cold call one board: which device did you use?

items.text: Please think about maybe using less plastic if you can.
It is important that everybody walks to school more often.
Polar bears need the sea ice, so we should try to protect it.
We should all turn off the lights whenever we leave a room.

say: These slogans are way too long.
Shrink each one to 8 words or fewer. Make it catchy.
trap: cutting words but keeping it boring: Use less plastic please.
Fix: student adds a pattern: repeat, rhyme or a question.
notes.stretch: Use rhyme or repetition in every slogan.
notes.help: Start with the key noun: plastic, walk, ice, lights.
notes.prep: Guided shrinking. Devices from Session 2 reappear. SC2.

slides.title: Which is the best call to action?
slides.prompt: Poster: stop plastic bottles at our school

options.misconception: too big to act on; nobody knows what to do next

notes.answer: B - one small, clear thing to do, with a when
beats: SAY: A call to action tells the reader exactly what to do next.
ASK: Which is the best call to action?
10 sec. Cue: voices off, everyone points to A, B or C.
EXPECT: pointing to B
SCAN the room, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, cold call: what job does C do?
Less -> ask could you do it tomorrow? for each, re-ask.
REVEAL after pointing is scanned.
SAY: B. Small, clear, and it says when. You can do it tomorrow.
trap: pointing to A because it's the biggest goal.
Fix: ask what would you actually do at 9 am? Student re-chooses.
notes.prep: Decision point before designing. Under 80% means every student writes their call to action on a board for a check before starting.

slides.title: Design your campaign poster
slides.task: Work through your Worksheet, plan your poster on it, then make your A3 campaign poster.
slides.frame: My picture shows ___, and my slogan says ___.

notes.answer: a poster with all four parts on one message
beats: POINT to the task.
SAY: Plan first, then draw. The planner takes 5 minutes; the poster takes the rest.
SAY: Read the task, complete each part, check your work.
Finished? Extension next. Everyone, together, on three.
CIRCULATE. Ask: what's your one message? Does your picture show it?
ASK: Hold your planner up. Are all four parts filled in?
5 sec. Cue: Fingers at your chest, how many parts done... show me.
EXPECT: 4 before starting on A3
TIME 22 minutes. At 20, posters up on the wall.
trap: spending the whole time drawing, slogan squeezed in at the end.
Fix: student writes the slogan on the A3 first, then draws.
notes.stretch: Extension: one message for three readers, then a second poster.
notes.help: Supported Worksheet: picture-clue choices, a first slogan done, a planning frame.
notes.prep: Fun activity: draw and create. Posters can go up around the school during Week 5 publishing. SC2 and SC3.

slides.extendedTask: a worksheet ending in a poster plan, then an A3 campaign poster

slides.title: Gallery walk: would you stop?
lines: Walk the gallery. Read each poster for two seconds.
Sticky note: one star (what works) and one action you'd take.

notes.answer: open - notes name a part that works and the action
beats: SAY: Two seconds per poster. That's all a real poster gets.
CIRCULATE with the class. Read notes as they go up.
ASK: Which poster made you stop first?
10 sec. Cue: voices off, everyone points to it... now.
EXPECT: a few posters get most points
ASK: Why did that one work? Name a part.
15 sec. Turn and tell, partner B first.
EXPECT: the picture told the story; the slogan was short
trap: notes that say nice or cool.
Fix: model one note: Your slogan rhymes, I'll bring a bottle.
notes.prep: Peer feedback rehearsal before Week 5's feedback session. 6 minutes. SC3.

slides.title: Show what you know
questions: New campaign: stop litter on the beach.
Write a slogan (8 words or fewer) and a call to action.

notes.answer: e.g. Leave only footprints. Take three pieces of rubbish home
beats: SAY: A brand new campaign. Slogan and action, go.
ASK: Write a slogan and a call to action.
60 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: a short catchy slogan; a small, clear action
RECORD who writes a claim as the action. Week 4 drafting conference.
trap: Litter is bad. as the call to action.
Fix: none now, record the name.
notes.prep: Exit evidence for SC2 on a new campaign. One board per student.

slides.reflectionPrompt: What's one thing from your poster you'll use in your big persuasive piece next week?

notes.answer: open - slogan as title, the fact, the action as the ending
beats: SAY: Let's read our I can lines together. Everyone, together, on three.
ASK: How sure are you that your words and picture work together?
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs up, sideways or down
RECORD each thumb down beside the exit boards.
ASK: What from your poster will you use in your big piece?
20 sec. Turn and tell, partner A first.
EXPECT: my slogan as my title; my call to action as my ending
notes.prep: Self-assessment read beside the exit boards. Week 4 starts the big piece: issue, audience and form. SC2.
